arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argued that Colorado's law restricts speech based on content and viewpoint and must survive strict scrutiny under the First Amendment.
the opposing side argued that state power is at its apex when regulating healthcare professions to ensure safety, making the law a valid exercise of police power.

Justice Sotomayor questioned whether a law on the books alone creates a chilling effect or whether an imminent threat of prosecution is required. Justice Sotomayor also asked the side that brought the case to define talk therapy and whether Colorado disavows enforcement of that kind of treatment.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Kaley Chiles, a counselor, challenges a Colorado law that prohibits helping minors pursue state-disfavored goals on gender and sexuality. The state defends the law as a healthcare safety regulation.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Sotomayor asked whether merely having a law on the books creates a chilling effect, or whether there must be an imminent and credible threat of prosecution.

Justice Sotomayor asked the side that brought the case to define talk therapy and whether Colorado disavows enforcement of that kind of treatment. Justice Sotomayor also asked about the opposite sex in counseling context. Justice Thomas asked whether Colorado argued below that the law only prohibits treatments seeking to change a minor's sexual orientation or gender identity because they are unsafe and ineffective.
